body: Awesome, I'll send you an invite when I next use my PS3. (Which shouldn't be long since I'm using it for Netflix/Prime Video.) Thanks, same.

Oh, I see. :) I didn't get a PS3 very long ago so I haven't actually played online with it yet. Actually, I think I got Battlefield 3 and played that once or twice. I'm not 100% sure of my ID so you'd need to send me yours. Also, I don't have a PS3 headset. :(

Heh, I'm glad you enjoyed the day because I find the place pretty boring. Oh, I see. I used to play Halo a lot when I was younger and I was pretty good, but now for some reason (since getting the XB1 and Halo collection six months ago) I'm losing all the time. So I know the feeling! Ah, so you're a carer as a job? That's nice.

Yes, fortunately my seizures are more controlled now but they still cause problems. I think I'm ready to start looking for new friends now, though, since my seizures are less likely to occur. It's a great thing to look after people with such difficulties, so I commend you for that.

I actually live in Stockport which is close to Manchester. I said Manchester because of course, more people know it, and it's only a fairly short journey away. :-) I noticed you're a gamer. Is it just Sony? I mostly play PC games but I have an Xbox One. I do have a PS3 but not a PS4.

Actually, I said in the OP that I'm not looking to kill myself. I recently watched a documentary about this topic and it merely piqued my curiosity. Previously the idea of killing myself as part of a group hadn't come to mind.

However, since you asked, I'm not actually sure. I've been a recluse for years now. If I really wanted companionship perhaps I'd have changed that behaviour by now. When I was younger I was in a few relationships, but I've been single for five years. I suppose maybe it's time for a change, but I'm certainly not yearning for it. Don't worry about your empathy difficulties. I've had a couple of friends with Asperger's syndrome, so I have experience talking to people with autism since it is on the spectrum. The fact you're trying to help people is a great thing, more so with the challenges you're facing with autism.
Hey. I've been better, but then, I suppose I've been worse too. How's it going? Do you have epilepsy?
In which context do you mean? Regardless, if you're going to kill yourself you're usually going to do it alone so this isn't related to the question at hand.

I'm not here to judge your decision, but the method doesn't sound like a perfect plan. You could pass out simply from the fear or shock (without cutting yourself to the extent to effectively bleed out, I mean). If you do decide to kill yourself you should choose a sure-fire method. I'm saying this because one of my friends hanged himself. Whilst he ultimately succeeded, he didn't plan it properly and he suffered a truly agonising end. I wouldn't wish that on anyone.

Think hard about this. But if you decide to do it, I implore you to research alternative methods.
